prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the main manufacturing processes, production systems, and organization of industrial production.
Basic knowledge of CNC programming, computer-aided manufacturing, and application of IT tools to machining and production processes.
Basic knowledge of statistics applied to data analysis, process control, and performance evaluation in industrial environments.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Ability to program, manage and optimize flexible manufacturing cells in mechanical environments.

syllabus_topics: Design and management techniques for an FMS
assessment_rules: To pass by progressive evaluation, students must attend mandatory lab practices and group work, score at least 4/10 on the First and Second Progressive Exams, and achieve an overall combined average (NMC) of at least 5/10. Students who do not meet these progressive requirements or wish to improve their grade may take a Global Exam in the ordinary call, which can replace the scores of specific progressive exams while retaining passed parts; mandatory lab attendance is still required, and a final NMC of at least 5/10 with individual exam parts (PP1/PG1, PP2/PG2) scoring at least 4/10 is needed. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is 100% based on a single written exam, which requires a minimum score of 5/10 and mandatory lab practice attendance.
